policy: Evidence-led density: historical urbanization, maritime and commercial density, administrative complexity, routes, warfare and gameplay needs determine coverage; regional ranges are planning expectations, never equal polity quotas.

acceptedVariance.rationale: The 156 physically authored centres already preserve the dense capital, fortified, river and maritime hierarchy across the finalized Europe terrain packages; adding 24 low-distinction objects would reduce map readability and breach the locked meaningful-settlement rule.

factors: Nile, Maghreb and Sahelian urban networks
large sparsely urbanized areas use selective coverage

acceptedVariance.rationale: The 118 authored centres emphasize the Ming administrative and canal network, Korean and Japanese urban systems, ports and frontier nodes while explicitly retaining mobile steppe and Amur communities in authoritative abstract state; the planning minimum is not converted into invented towns.

Ten additional centres preserve distinct evidenced Mesoamerican, Andean, riverine, coastal and island networks rather than collapsing them into modern-border substitutes; the global catalogue remains within its locked range and runtime objects remain activation-bounded.

importanceExpectations.major: Broad capital, provincial, commercial, military, route and port coverage supported by evidence.
importanceExpectations.regional: Capital plus the polity's evidenced regional centers and gameplay-critical nodes.
importanceExpectations.local: Historically meaningful centers without a forced minimum; abstract communities are valid when physical representation adds little.

evidenceSources.scope: locked global density and compression rules
authored identities, placement, roles, ports and routes
